title: Quotes backend: lead-subordinate creation, versioning, quote operations with cascades, closed-record corrections
objective: Port the quote domain: quotes exist only under a lead, version discipline with one current version, the full quote operation set (assign, send, revise, mark-won with sibling withdrawal + lead Closed Won, mark-lost, withdraw), draft-vs-revise editing rules, and read-only-after-close with audited corrections (P-07 quote side, P-09).
scope: POST /api/v1/leads/{id}/quotes (create draft v1 — the quotes card is the sole creation point), GET quote list per lead, GET /api/v1/quotes/{id}, PUT draft update

POST /api/v1/quotes/{id}/operations/{op}: assign, send (valid-until + next-follow-up requirements), revise (new current version), mark-won (bound premium + decision date -> sibling open quotes withdrawn + lead Closed Won), mark-lost (structured reason, optional lead close), withdraw
Quote legality matrix (pure module, reporting category + canonical key) + availableOperations
quote_status_history append-only with actor/inputs; audit; automatic expiry excluded (job in T-032)
Closed-record read-only enforcement with audited corrections path per reference
Validation: valid-until > sent, sent >= received, decision >= sent unless exception recorded, premiums > 0, future next-follow-up while open past Quote Sent

Close the quotes.is_current invariant gap inherited from T-005 (evaluator ruling): add a NEW migration creating `unique index uq_quotes_current on quotes (tenant_id, lead_id) where is_current = true`, add the paired allow-list entry + target-only side-assertion in schema-business-dotnet-parity.test.ts, and refresh the db:validate snapshot via --update-snapshot. Never edit an already-applied migration - the snapshot enforces this.

Quote-side high-value pricing gate (re-scoped from AC-049/V-063 by human ruling on T-025-N1): quote Send requires pricing_approval_state=approved when the tenant gate is enabled AND the CURRENT QUOTE VERSION's quoted premium exceeds the tenant threshold; otherwise 422 PRICING_APPROVAL_REQUIRED with nothing persisted. Port from SendQuoteCommandHandler.cs:85-91 - measure it, do not infer it from this sentence.
implementation_details: Port QuoteOperationExecutor: transactions cover quote mutation + version management + sibling cascade + lead transition + history (both quote and lead where cascades touch the lead) + audit.
Version discipline: revise-after-send creates a new current version; exactly one is_current per quote enforced (constraint from T-005 + service logic).
Closed Won reachable ONLY via quote-level mark-won (P-07) — lead legality matrix has no direct Closed Won operation.
Corrections: closed quotes/leads editable only through the audited corrections capability with its own permission (spec 13 sensitive operations).
Executor exposes the same domain-event seam as T-025 for T-034 targeted re-evaluation.
Quoted premium derivation (current version) stays query-computed per section 11.

quotes.is_current gap: the .NET reference enforces one-current-quote only in application code, so concurrent operations can commit two current quotes and double-count premium in every dashboard joining is_current (same class as uq_quote_versions_current, ratified in T-005). T-026 owns every code path writing quotes.is_current, so the guard belongs here. The backfill caveat documented in the quotes migration header is a no-op locally (A-1: no production data, clean resets) but must be honoured for any deployed environment created before this index lands.

unit: Quote legality matrix table-driven parity; version-selection rule (one current)
integration: Create draft v1 under lead; draft edit allowed, post-send edit rejected (revise required); revise produces new current version
Send validations (valid-until, next-follow-up); mark-won cascades (siblings withdrawn, lead Closed Won, bound premium recorded); mark-lost with optional lead close; withdraw
History rows on quote and lead sides; audit entries; corrections path permission-bound + audited; illegal op 409 with hint
Tenant isolation; every quote belongs to exactly one lead (FK + API shape)
e2e: Quote panel/workflow specs adapted in T-043

findings.summary: CONTRADICTION (task file vs reference): the scope's operation list omits set-current, but the reference has it as a seventh operation with its own dedicated route POST /quotes/{id}/set-current (NOT under /operations/, QuoteEndpoints.cs:47), its own permission quotes.set_current, and a matrix row. It is also the only writer of quotes.is_current besides create - the exact column whose new invariant this task was amended to own. Implemented per the reference; flagged rather than silently added or silently omitted. | RESOLVED by evaluator ruling: the reference wins. Verified QuoteEndpoints.cs:47 first-hand - POST /quotes/{id}/set-current is a dedicated route NOT under /operations/, permission quotes.set_current (PermissionCatalog.cs:119, seeded in seed.sql:101). The TS port registers the same non-/operations/ path with the same permission and pins the DB-level one-current-per-lead guarantee (tests at quote-workflow.test.ts:1052-1105). Implementing it was correct: it is the only writer of quotes.is_current besides create, the exact column the task was amended to guard.

CONTRADICTION (AC-055 vs reference): AC-055 says update attempts on a closed lead/quote via normal endpoints fail 409, and refers to a separate corrections route. Measured: UpdateDraftQuoteCommandHandler.cs:73-85 answers 403 QUOTE_CLOSED_REQUIRES_CORRECTION_PERMISSION for a closed quote when the caller lacks quotes.correct_closed, and SUCCEEDS when they hold it - the PUT route IS the audited corrections path, and no separate corrections endpoint exists anywhere in QuoteEndpoints. 409 QUOTE_DRAFT_EDIT_ONLY is the answer for a Sent/Revised (non-draft, non-closed) quote instead. Ported per the reference, which also keeps the quote side consistent with the lead side T-024 already shipped (LEAD_CLOSED_REQUIRES_CORRECTION_PERMISSION -> 403).

CONTRADICTION (AC-054 vs reference): AC-054 requires mark-won to require bound premium and decision date (422 otherwise). Measured: both are OPTIONAL in MarkQuoteWonCommandHandler.cs:66-71 - boundPremium defaults to the CURRENT VERSION's quoted premium and decisionDate defaults to today; MarkQuoteWonValidator only constrains boundPremium to > 0 WHEN supplied. Ported per the reference (both optional, both defaulted) and asserted as such.

CONTRADICTION (AC-054/scope vs reference): AC-054 and this task's scope require date-order rules sent >= received and decision >= sent unless exception recorded. A grep of every date comparison across Features/Quotes finds only TWO date rules in the whole quote domain: preparedDate >= lead.dateReceived (CreateQuoteCommandHandler.cs:99) and validUntil > sentDate (SendQuoteCommandHandler.cs:72). There is no sent-vs-received rule and no decision-vs-sent rule, and no exception-recorded mechanism exists anywhere in the reference. The two real rules are implemented and tested; the two nonexistent ones are NOT invented. FLAGGED for a human ruling rather than filled in.

MEASURED, counter-intuitive, and pinned by its own test: quote creation does NOT cascade a NEW lead to Pricing. QuoteLeadCascade.MoveLeadToPricingIfPreQuotingAsync guards on LeadWorkflow.IsLegal(StartPricing, ...), and the lead matrix allows start-pricing only from Assigned/Information Gathering/Underwriting (LeadWorkflow.cs:104-109) - so a quote raised against a brand-new unassigned lead leaves it in New. My first draft of the integration test assumed the naive reading (pre-Pricing lead moves to Pricing) and went red; the CODE was right and the TEST was wrong. Both directions are now pinned explicitly. | RESOLVED: verified the cascade guard reasoning against LeadWorkflow and confirmed both directions are pinned (quote-workflow.test.ts:782 cascade from Assigned, :802 explicit no-cascade from New).

MEASURED list-envelope shape: GET /leads/{id}/quotes returns a BARE ARRAY of QuoteListItemDto, not the {items,totalCount} envelope used by the paged list endpoints (QuoteEndpoints.cs:60-65 returns Results.Ok(IReadOnlyList<...>)). Checked rather than assumed, per the standing warning that the totalCount rule does not hold universally. It is a lead-subordinate card with no paging/filter/sort parameters, so there is no total to report. Preserved as-is. | RESOLVED: verified QuoteEndpoints.cs:60-65 returns Results.Ok(IReadOnlyList<QuoteListItemDto>) - a bare array, no {items,totalCount} envelope - and the TS list endpoint asserts Array.isArray (quote-workflow.test.ts:777). Checked rather than assumed, correctly.

DOC-vs-CODE divergence inside the reference itself: QuoteOperationExecutor's doc comment (:20-24) claims it checks the closed-quote-correction gate as a defensive second gate, but the executor's actual code contains no CorrectClosed check at all. The comment even concedes it is structurally impossible today since every QuoteWorkflow rule already excludes every terminal status. Followed the CODE: the correction gate lives only on the PUT path. Closed quotes are still unreachable by every workflow operation via the legality matrix, asserted for all seven operations. | RESOLVED by evaluator ruling: following the CODE over the stale doc comment was correct. The executor contains no CorrectClosed check; every workflow rule already excludes terminal statuses, and the port asserts closed quotes reject all seven operations (quote-workflow.test.ts:1728).

FIXED A FIXTURE DEFECT IN ANOTHER TASK'S FILE, caused by this task's migration: lead-workflow.test.ts's seedQuote() hard-coded is_current=true, so any test seeding several quotes on one lead created TWO current quotes - a state production cannot reach and that double-counts premium in every dashboard joining quote.is_current. The new uq_quotes_current index rejects it, which is how it surfaced. Changed to current-only-if-the-lead-has-no-current-quote-yet, matching CreateQuoteCommandHandler. Nothing in that suite asserts is_current; all 40 of its tests pass. This is a direct consequence of MY change, not a sibling artifact, so it was fixed rather than reported. | RESOLVED by evaluator ruling: fixing the sibling fixture was the right call. The failure was mechanically caused by this task's own uq_quotes_current index; the fixture seeded a state production cannot reach (two current quotes, premium double-counting); the fix ('current only if the lead has no current quote yet', lead-workflow.test.ts:300-321) matches CreateQuoteCommandHandler semantics; nothing in that suite asserts is_current. Evaluator re-ran the suite serially: 40/40 pass. This also resolves T-048's F-048-3.

DEFERRED TO THE ORCHESTRATOR (deliberate, per brief): the scope asks for a db:validate snapshot refresh via --update-snapshot, but the brief forbids running db:validate / supabase:reset against the shared local DB. The new migration 20260719001000_quotes_current_guard.sql was applied with the non-destructive npm run db:migrate, and the parity allow-list entry plus its automatic side-assertion are in place. The snapshot refresh still needs to be run serially by the orchestrator. | RESOLVED: the orchestrator ran the snapshot refresh serially, reviewed the full diff before accepting it (exactly the guard: uq_quotes_current, its COMMENT, the default-partition index, the ATTACH PARTITION; 2380 -> 2388 lines), and db:validate now exits 0.

NO ORDERING FLAKE OBSERVED in this task's quote_status_history assertions across roughly a dozen full runs of the suite. Quote history deliberately reuses the lead side's appendQuoteStatusHistory (leads/workflow/history.ts) and the same (acted_at, id) read ordering rather than defining a divergent writer, so whatever T-048 lands for the lead-side root cause covers the quote side through the shared pattern. Nothing was worked around locally. | RESOLVED: T-048 landed the root-cause fix and the quote side is covered through the shared pattern - listQuoteStatusHistory (quotes/repository.ts:702) orders by the identity column id, not forked. One residue remains in this task's TEST helper only, filed separately as T-026-E1.

EVALUATOR (tests-code-review): readQuoteHistory in quote-workflow.test.ts:481-488 reintroduces the T-048 alias-shadowing mechanism on its TIE-BREAK key. The helper selects `id::text as id` and sorts with a bare `order by acted_at, id`: acted_at is NOT aliased (the primary key sorts the real timestamptz), but the bare `id` tie-break resolves to the TEXT alias, so two rows of one quote sharing an identical acted_at would tie-break as strings ('10' < '9' across a digit-length boundary). Verified first-hand that Postgres resolves the bare name to the alias. Latent rare flake of exactly the class T-048 eradicated (this file landed AFTER T-048's repo scan, so T-048's 'no other occurrences' claim was true when made). Fix is one line: qualify the tie-break (e.g. `order by acted_at, quote_status_history.id`) or drop the acted_at key and order by the qualified id alone, matching the lead-side helper. Test-only; production listQuoteStatusHistory is correct (orders by id).

EVALUATOR (tracking): the uq_quotes_current index is a documented TARGET-ONLY DEVIATION (absent from the .NET reference, where the invariant lived only in the handlers) and per the orchestrator must enter the AC-095 deviation ledger at T-044 - but T-044's task file currently contains no mention of it (verified: zero occurrences of 'uq_quotes_current' or 'deviation' in .claude/tasks/T-044.json). The deviation itself is ratified (T-005 evaluator ruling 2, verified verbatim: 'fold into T-026 as a NEW migration + parity allow-list entry') and is self-documenting in the index COMMENT and the parity allow-list, but the ledger obligation needs to be recorded on T-044 by the orchestrator so it is not lost. No implementor action required on T-026.

OBLIGATION INHERITED FROM T-008 (evaluator, iteration 5, categorised as consumer-side not a T-008 finding): the money-type pins guarantee that `numeric` columns are typed string (never number) throughout the Kysely schema, on Select/Insert/Update. That guarantee is bypassable from consumer code via raw `sql<number>` casts. When this task reads, aggregates or writes premium/threshold values, do NOT cast money to number - keep it string and do arithmetic in SQL (numeric) or with an explicit decimal-safe path. The T-008 pin cannot catch a cast written here. Background: this pin was defeated SIX times during T-008 (three vacuity axes, sampling, nullability mismatch, write-path), so treat money typing as a known-fragile area and assert it in this task's own tests.
